title: Execution targets and rebind
summary: Frozen targets and digests stay as provenance across authorized takeover and never gate a write. Current execution ownership, same-target ancestry, tenant/project/member or shared-group authority and endpoint checks remain required. QA tests whatever is deployed: QA start reports a different served commit and proceeds, and every deployment-bound browser case records the commit its environment served at case start. Once the successor has a ready deploy receipt, execution and mission views name its release_lineage and, for a pinned target, its release_version, without rewriting the stored target or digest, and command cases check out the current owning run's project source. A takeover tells each moved member owner once that QA moved to the successor and opens at its item QA stage; the predecessor wake is not the command. An owner whose carried walk is still open under a live session gets no takeover notice and no successor stage wake: the walk keeps going and may pass on the newer build. A member with live item QA stays attached during rework set-aside passes. Once its execution stops being live, the next pass sets the member aside if it is still reworking, preserving its QA history. While a case still carries the target its fail answered, an inherited fail whose latest failing attempt was created before this run, and whose merge is in the current release, retries with yoke qa plan run --item REF --stage STAGE --project SLUG; any other fail on the current target gets the ordinary rework handoff. Materialization rebinds open private and run QA requirements in place to the successor receipt, keeping each case ID and prior target JSON. A predecessor pass carries only across the same destination, including repeated takeovers; otherwise the case is owed again. A fail or other non-pass recorded against the previous target does not count against the rebound one: red-requirement reads, stage grading and the driver's pending-plan selection share one predicate that treats it as not yet run, so the steering report does not flag the run and the driver captures an automatic plan again when the run reaches that stage. An open shared plan group keeps its group identity, pinned cases and case IDs, and once its owning run holds a newer ready receipt (after takeover or a redeploy) dispatch or the next group run rebinds every live group case to that target, carrying same-destination passes; a group whose walk has begun keeps its target. Begun executions and captures keep their frozen targets, and a walk whose requirement was rebound keeps running host commands and walk-end against its frozen case while a changed definition, position or starting run still refuses; an execution that has run, leased and recorded nothing, such as one waiting for its Test Machine turn, takes the successor's current roster and target when its owner begins it again or the host-turn wake resumes it by execution id, keeping its execution ID, execution_order and host-line place, for member executions and plan-group walks alike. If begin sees a changed roster for a frozen walk in walking or awaiting_walk_review, qa_walk_in_progress directs the owner to finish any outstanding walk-end and submit review on the existing execution. When a walk completes before the successor reaches the QA stage, rebinding credits its saved pass if the frozen target belongs to the run lineage and the destination matches. A run started on the previous target and completed after the rebind is credited the same way when its verdict settles: it must be the case's latest attempt, record the stored previous target's digest and pass on the same destination, and it keeps that attribution. Neither observation changes nor early verdicts grant release approval. Manual-only takeover notices tell holders without a future scheduled wake to check the evidence and schedule their next recheck before parking; no dispatch wakes them for it. Steering recipients must staff the item for that check. Holders with future scheduled rechecks receive no manual-only takeover notice; automatic or mixed requirements keep successor dispatch guidance.
